findings.title: Cleanup job interval changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: The PR changes the CleanUpService ticker from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`. This runs the entire cleanup suite (tmp files, expired snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, query history) ten times more frequently. Nothing in the PR description mentions this, so it looks like an accidental debug leftover. If intentional it needs justification, since jobs like query-history row-limit enforcement and annotation cleanup now execute every minute against the production database.

findings.title: Routine cleanup progress logged at Error level with full ID lists
findings.body: CleanAnnotations, CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags now call `r.log.Error("Annotations to clean by time", ..., "ids", ids, ...)` (and three similar calls) for normal, successful operation. These fire on every batch of every cleanup cycle, emitting error-severity log lines (which typically trigger alerting/dashboards on error counts) and dumping the full list of up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize IDs into the logs. These should be Debug level at most; as written they will spam error logs in production.

findings.title: SQLite ID list built with quadratic string concatenation
findings.body: In deleteByIDs, the SQLite fallback builds the IN clause via `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` in a loop, which copies the whole accumulated string each iteration — O(n²) work. The new test uses a batch size of 32767, so this builds strings totaling hundreds of thousands of bytes through ~32k reallocations. strings.Builder or bytes.Buffer would make it linear.
